name: Offsite and unit auxiliary power (switchyard to 6.9 kV bus incomers)
notes: REBASED 2026-09-06: plant reference changed from US EPR to a late-1990s Westinghouse 4-loop PWR. Replaces the old rcp.json upstream chain (SWYD-400KV -> NAT-1/2 -> NBUS-1/2), which fed house load straight from the grid and had no generator connection. US practice: the unit feeds its own auxiliaries from its own generator through unit auxiliary transformers tapped off the isolated phase bus, with a reserve transformer off the switchyard as the offsite source, and an automatic scheme that swings each bus from one to the other. SCOPE: offsite only. Onsite power (4.16 kV Class 1E buses, EDGs, 480 V load centers/MCCs, AAC diesel) is NOT designed yet - see eps/onsite.json when it lands. NBUS-{n} is defined here so this file is self-contained and drawable, tagged migrateTo EPS-ONSITE. DESIGN FORK TAKEN: this plant HAS a generator breaker (already implemented client-side as the 'Gen Breaker' switch), so the UATs sit on the generator side of it, startup power comes from the RAT, and the operator performs a manual live-parallel back-transfer to normal after synchronizing. At plants without a generator breaker auxiliaries backfeed from the grid through the MSUT and no startup transfer is needed. NAMING EXCEPTION: MSUT/UAT/RAT keep their universal industry names instead of the feeds-rule -XFMR form, so they match UFSAR Ch 8 wording - see _schema.md. All numerics approx pending a real UFSAR Ch 8 (Watts Bar, Vogtle, Callaway, Comanche Peak, Seabrook are public). Switchyard modeled as a single node - ring bus / breaker-and-a-half detail deferred. All MCR controls here are LATCHING (Rot2p/Rot3p) and use the out-of-correspondence convention; no spring-return controller exists yet.

devices.name: 345kV switchyard (grid source)
devices.behavior: Grid connection and the plant's offsite power source. Feeds RAT directly and receives unit output through MSUT. Deenergized = loss of offsite power: RAT dies, and if the generator is not carrying the house load the normal buses go dead and the RCPs coast down on their flywheels. Single node - individual switchyard breakers, the ring bus and the second incoming line are deferred.

devices.name: Main step-up transformer (MSUT, generator to switchyard)
devices.behavior: Steps generator voltage up to the switchyard. Carries the full unit output outbound; with GEN-52 closed and the generator off the line it also backfeeds the isolated phase bus from the grid, which keeps the UATs alive. Faulted isolates the unit from the grid entirely: no export path and no backfeed. Its own protection (87T, sudden pressure) is deferred to the turbine-generator file.

devices.name: Generator breaker (GEN-52)
devices.behavior: Ties the isolated phase bus to MSUT and thus the switchyard. Closed by the operator at the end of the synchronizing sequence (synchroscope + sync-check), opened on generator or turbine trip. Its trip contact is the fast-transfer initiate signal for both normal buses. Already implemented client-side as the 'Gen Breaker' switch; the synchronizing sequence itself belongs to the turbine-generator file. At plants with no generator breaker the same function sits on the switchyard line breaker - identical from the panel.

devices.name: Isolated phase bus (generator / MSUT / UAT node)
devices.behavior: Generator-voltage bus between the generator terminals, the UAT taps and GEN-52. THE node that makes the plant feed itself: energized when the generator is excited, or backfed from the grid when GEN-52 is closed with the generator off the line. Dies when the generator trips and GEN-52 opens - which is the event the whole transfer scheme exists to catch.

devices.name: Unit auxiliary transformer {uat} (UAT-{uat}, feeds NBUS-{uat})
devices.behavior: Taps the isolated phase bus on the GENERATOR side of GEN-52 and steps 22kV down to 6.9kV for its normal bus. The normal source at power - the unit supplies its own auxiliaries. In-service but dead whenever IPB is dead (generator offline and GEN-52 open), which is why startup runs on the reserve transformer. Internal fault picks up UAT-{uat}-PROT and locks out, holding the normal incomer open until the lockout is reset locally.

devices.name: UAT {uat} protection package (UAT-{uat}-87T/-51/-63)
devices.behavior: 87T transformer differential (instantaneous), 51 time overcurrent backup, 63 sudden-pressure from the tank. Any element latches UAT-{uat}-86. A UAT fault is both a trip and a transfer initiate: the bus must go to reserve, and it must NOT come back until the lockout is reset.

devices.name: UAT {uat} lockout relay (UAT-{uat}-86)
devices.behavior: Latches on UAT-{uat}-PROT pickup: trips NBUS-{uat}-NORM-52, holds it open, initiates the fast transfer to reserve, and blocks any back-transfer. Manual local reset only, after the fault is investigated - so a UAT lockout parks the bus on reserve for the rest of the scenario.

devices.name: Reserve auxiliary transformer (RAT, feeds RBUS)
devices.behavior: Fed directly from the switchyard, steps 345kV down to 6.9kV onto the reserve bus. The offsite source: startup and shutdown power, and the destination of every automatic transfer. Normally energized with both reserve incomers open (hot standby). Single RAT is deliberate - it makes the reserve path a genuine single point of failure, so a RAT lockout plus a generator trip is a real station blackout path rather than a bookkeeping exercise.

devices.name: RAT protection package (RAT-87T/-51/-63)
devices.behavior: 87T differential, 51 backup overcurrent, 63 sudden pressure on the reserve transformer. Pickup latches RAT-86.

devices.name: RAT lockout relay (RAT-86)
devices.behavior: Latches on RAT-PROT pickup: trips BOTH reserve incomers, deenergizes RBUS and blocks every automatic transfer on both buses. With the reserve path locked out, a subsequent generator trip loses all four RCPs. Manual local reset only.

devices.name: 6.9kV reserve bus (RBUS)
devices.behavior: Reserve 6.9kV bar off the RAT secondary, tapped by the reserve incomer of every normal bus. Energized iff SWYD-345KV energized, RAT in-service and RAT-86 reset. Its health is the single thing that decides whether a fast transfer has anywhere to go.

devices.name: Bus {n} normal incomer breaker (NBUS-{n}-NORM-52)
devices.behavior: Connects UAT-{uat} to NBUS-{n}. Closed for the whole run at power; open at startup because the generator is not yet carrying the house load. Tripped by the transfer scheme, by UAT-{uat}-86, or by the MCR control switch. Electrically interlocked with NBUS-{n}-RES-52: the pair may only be closed together momentarily, under sync-check supervision, during a manual back-transfer.

devices.name: Bus {n} reserve incomer breaker (NBUS-{n}-RES-52)
devices.behavior: Connects RBUS to NBUS-{n}. The startup lineup closes it; the automatic transfer closes it; the operator opens it at the end of a manual back-transfer. Tripped by RAT-86 or by its own overcurrent protection. Same interlock with NORM-52 - break-before-make for every automatic transfer.

devices.name: Bus {n} voltage transformers (NBUS-{n}-VT)
devices.behavior: VT set on NBUS-{n}. Feeds the 27 undervoltage elements, the 81 underfrequency element, one side of the 25 sync-check, and the panel voltmeter and frequency meter. Failed VTs are why a transfer scheme can sit blind while the bus dies - worth modeling as a casualty.

devices.name: Bus {n} undervoltage relays (NBUS-{n}-27)
devices.behavior: Two elements on one device. 'degraded' at about 90% of nominal with a short delay: an independent fast-transfer initiate for cases where no trip contact arrives (a UAT fault the differential misses, an upstream open). 'residual' below about 30%: the permissive that lets a failed fast transfer fall back to a residual-voltage transfer once the coasting motors have stopped holding the bus up. Also drives the BUS UNDERVOLTAGE annunciator.

devices.name: Bus {n} underfrequency relay (NBUS-{n}-81)
devices.behavior: Underfrequency on an RCP bus. In a Westinghouse plant this is a hardwired REACTOR TRIP input (RCP bus underfrequency, above the low-power interlock) - the reactor is tripped before loop flow decays with a sagging grid, because the RCPs are fixed-speed and simply follow the bus. Pickup here alarms and hands the signal to the future RPS file; it does not trip anything in this file. This is what the 0-80 Hz frequency gauges are actually indicating.

devices.name: Bus {n} incomer sync-check relay (NBUS-{n}-25)
devices.behavior: Supervises closing either incomer against the other. Compares voltage, frequency and phase angle across the two sources. 'dead-bus-ok' when the bus or the incoming source is dead - close freely, which is the normal automatic case. 'in-sync' when both sides are live and matched, which is what permits the momentary parallel of a manual back-transfer (both sources are tied to the same grid through the MSUT, so they are normally in step). 'blocked' otherwise, and the close command is physically inhibited.

devices.name: Bus {n} automatic transfer scheme (NBUS-{n}-XFER)
devices.behavior: The state machine that swings NBUS-{n} between its two sources. Break-before-make in every automatic case: trip the normal incomer, confirm it open on the 52b contact, then close the reserve incomer. Fast transfer completes in about 5-10 cycles, quick enough that motors ride through on residual voltage. If the fast path is unavailable it falls back to a residual-voltage transfer once NBUS-{n}-27 reads 'residual'; if the reserve incomer will not close or RBUS is dead it goes to 'failed' and the bus stays dead. 'blocked' is the MCR mode selector in OFF - no automatic action at all, which is how you set up a dead bus deliberately. Back-transfer to normal is never automatic.

devices.name: 6.9kV normal (non-1E) bus {n}
devices.behavior: Each normal bus feeds two RCP electrical groups (RCP1&2 on NBUS-1, RCP3&4 on NBUS-2) plus the balance-of-plant loads and load-center transformers that the onsite file will own. Energized from exactly one incomer at a time: (NORM-52 closed AND UAT-{uat} in-service AND IPB energized) OR (RES-52 closed AND RBUS energized). NOT backed by the emergency diesels - losing one bus loses two RCPs, which is the two-loop low-flow reactor trip.

signals.name: Grid frequency
signals.notes: Already implemented client-side as the 'Grid Freq.' gauge, 57-63 Hz.

signals.name: Bus {n} frequency
signals.notes: A real bus frequency meter is an expanded 55-65 Hz scale; 0-80 reuses the existing gauge asset and has the advantage of showing a dead bus decaying to zero.

signals.name: Bus {n} source (derived)
signals.expr: NBUS-{n}-NORM-52 == closed ? normal : (NBUS-{n}-RES-52 == closed ? reserve : dead)

signals.name: Bus {n} normal incomer out of correspondence (derived)
signals.notes: Latching-switch convention: the switch is a maintained request, so any trip leaves it disagreeing with the breaker. Drives the lamp mismatch and blocks reclosing until the switch is cycled.

signals.name: Bus {n} reserve incomer out of correspondence (derived)
Offsite power available (derived)
signals.expr: SWYD-345KV == energized AND RAT == in-service AND RAT-86 == reset

signals.name: Loss of offsite power (derived)
signals.notes: With a single RAT this is the only offsite path. A second incoming line / second reserve transformer would make this a 2-of-2 condition.

permissives.expr: IPB == energized AND UAT-{uat} == in-service AND UAT-{uat}-86 == reset AND (NBUS-{n}-RES-52 == open OR NBUS-{n}-25 == in-sync)
permissives.notes: The parallel case is the manual back-transfer: both sources live and in step, closed together for a moment. Everything else requires the other incomer open.

permissives.expr: RBUS == energized AND RAT-86 == reset AND (NBUS-{n}-NORM-52 == open OR NBUS-{n}-25 == in-sync)
permissives.notes: Automatic transfers always satisfy this through the NORM-52-open branch - break-before-make.
Synchronizing permissive owned by the turbine-generator file (synchroscope + sync-check). Listed here only because GEN-52 lives in this file.

autoActions.action: trip NBUS-{n}-NORM-52, then close NBUS-{n}-RES-52; NBUS-{n}-XFER -> reserve
autoActions.expr: NBUS-{n}-XFER == normal AND mcr:NBUS-{n}-XFER-MODE == auto AND (external:TURB-TRIP OR GEN-52 == tripped OR UAT-{uat}-86 == lockout OR NBUS-{n}-27 == degraded)
autoActions.notes: The fast (dead-bus) transfer. Close is supervised by the NORM-52 52b contact, not by a timer - never parallel the sources. Total dead time about 5-10 cycles; bus voltage dips to roughly 70-80% and recovers, motors ride through on residual voltage and the operator sees a blip and an annunciator.

autoActions.expr: NBUS-{n}-XFER == transferring AND NBUS-{n}-NORM-52 == open AND NBUS-{n}-27 == residual AND RBUS == energized
autoActions.notes: Fallback when the fast path never fired (no trip contact, VT failure, initiate lost) or the close was blocked. Waits for bus voltage to decay below ~30%, which takes 1-4 s with this much motor inertia on the bus. Every motor has slowed measurably by then: loop flow sags and the reactor may or may not survive it.

autoActions.expr: NBUS-{n}-XFER == transferring AND (RBUS == deenergized OR NBUS-{n}-RES-52 == tripped OR residualTimeoutS elapsed)
autoActions.notes: Bus stays dead. Two RCPs coast down on their flywheels, two-loop low flow trips the reactor, and the RCP auxiliary MCCs go looking for their alternate feed. Recovery is manual.
Trip and hold open; back-transfer blocked until the lockout is reset locally.
Loses the reserve path for the whole plant. Any bus already on reserve goes dead immediately.

sequences.trigger: turbine or generator trip, UAT lockout, or bus undervoltage at 90%, with the mode selector in AUTO
steps: NBUS-{n}-XFER -> transferring; BUS {n} TRANSFER annunciator
trip NBUS-{n}-NORM-52 (t = 0)
wait for the NORM-52 52b contact to confirm open (~30-50 ms)
close NBUS-{n}-RES-52 - total dead time 85-170 ms
NBUS-{n}-XFER -> reserve; BUS {n} ON RESERVE annunciator seals in
if RES-52 does not confirm closed, fall through to NBUS-{n}-RESIDUAL-XFER-SEQ

sequences.trigger: fast transfer unavailable or incomplete with NORM-52 already open
steps: hold with the bus coasting on motor residual voltage
wait for NBUS-{n}-27 to read residual (< ~30% of nominal, 1-4 s)
close NBUS-{n}-RES-52
re-accelerate the bus; RCP speed and loop flow recover from a visible sag
if residualTimeoutS elapses with no close, NBUS-{n}-XFER -> failed and the bus is dead

sequences.trigger: operator, after the generator is synchronized and loaded (never automatic)
steps: verify GEN-52 closed and the generator carrying load
verify UAT-{uat} in-service and UAT-{uat}-86 reset
verify NBUS-{n}-25 reads in-sync (both sources live, tied through the MSUT, so normally in step)
close NBUS-{n}-NORM-52 - momentary make-before-break parallel
verify the bus is carried from normal (incomer current shifts)
trip NBUS-{n}-RES-52
NBUS-{n}-XFER -> normal; return the reserve control switch to open to clear the out-of-correspondence lamp

sequences.trigger: cold plant initial condition (this file's initialState)
steps: SWYD-345KV energized, RAT in-service, RBUS energized
generator offline, GEN-52 open, IPB dead, both UATs in-service but dead
both NORM-52 open, both RES-52 closed, both buses energized from reserve
NBUS-{n}-XFER -> reserve; both ON RESERVE annunciators lit - normal for a shutdown plant
RCPs can be started on reserve power; back-transfer happens later, after the generator is on the line

control.notes: LATCHING - maintained request, not a momentary command. The breaker follows when the permissive is met; any trip leaves the switch out of correspondence and reclosing is blocked until it is cycled back to open. Rot2p exists in Unity.
SwitchLampIndicator exists; the both-lit state is the new one to add.
LATCHING, same convention as the normal incomer.

LATCHING three-position selector - a genuine maintained selector, which is what Rot3p is good for. OFF blocks the scheme entirely (deliberate dead-bus setups); MANUAL arms the scheme but requires the operator to close the reserve incomer; AUTO is the normal at-power position.
kV. GE-generic-gauge model available. Dedicated per-bus meters rather than one meter behind a selector switch, because a transfer is exactly when you want to watch both buses at once.
Hz. Same scale as the existing RCP frequency gauges - and now that pump speed follows the bus, they are indicating the same physical quantity.
kV. The one meter that tells the operator whether an automatic transfer has anywhere to go.
The control switch itself is already implemented client-side as 'Gen Breaker' and is owned by the turbine-generator panel; this is the position indication as seen from the electrical panel.
Also an RPS reactor-trip input - see NBUS-{n}-81.
First-out grade - this one wakes everybody up.
